question: Which of the following has NO effect on the resistance of a conductor?
solution:
The correct answer is **Shape.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Electrical Resistance**

 
 
• **​**The following factors influence a conductor's **electrical resistance**:

 
 
• The **cross-sectional area** of the conductor
 
• **Length** of the conductor
 
• The **material **of the conductor
 
• The** temperature **of the conducting material
 
 
 
• Electrical resistance is** inversely proportional **to the conductor's cross-sectional area **(A)** and directly proportional to its length **(L)**. The relationship that follows provides it.
 
• **R= **** ρL/A**, where ρ is the material's resistivity, expressed as **m/ohm meter**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistivity**

 
 
• At a particular temperature, the electrical resistivity, which is denoted by ρ, is defined as the electrical resistance offered **per unit length and unit cross-sectional area.**
 
• Specific electrical resistance is another term for electrical resistance. **Electrical resistivity** is measured in **m** by the SI.
 
• The ability of a material to** resist the flow of an electric current **is measured qualitatively by its resistivity. It goes without saying that the resistivity of** insulators will be higher** than that of conductors.
 
• The resistivities of a few different materials are compared below. Materials with a **low resistivity are excellent conductors of electricity.**
 
 
• Silver – 1.00×10−⁸
 
• Copper – 1.68×10−⁸
 
• Aluminum – 2.82×10−⁸
 
• Wood – 1.00×10¹⁴
 
• Air – 2.30×10¹⁶
 
• Teflon – 1.00×10²³
